**Normal behavior:**

- Echo writes text or binary to standard output by default, with a trailing newline unless suppressed. It can write to standard error instead. It is robust to misconfigured terminals where ordinary printing of Unicode would fail: on a standard stream whose declared encoding is ASCII-only, echo writes the text encoded as UTF-8 instead of failing or dropping characters. It never adds styles to plain text. When the stream is not a terminal, ANSI styles in the text are stripped; when it is a terminal, styles are kept. The invocation may force color on (styles kept even when the stream is not a terminal), force color off (styles stripped even on a terminal), or leave autodetection; echo follows the color flag of the context current on its thread, and a thread that has not entered the context autodetects.
↳ N-000609–N-000617

- Styling wraps text with ANSI styles. Named foreground/background colors are the finite set: black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white, bright_black, bright_red, bright_green, bright_yellow, bright_blue, bright_magenta, bright_cyan, bright_white, and reset; a background color is styled differently from the same foreground color, and different names are styled differently. Color may also be an integer in 0–255 inclusive or a sequence of exactly three integers each in 0–255 inclusive (RGB). Independent style switches: bold, dim, underline, overline, italic, blink, reverse, strikethrough; each switch changes the styling, and a combination of switches differs from each switch alone. By default a reset is appended so styles do not leak. Any other color value fails the style call; that call does not succeed as if the color was omitted. Styled echo is echo plus styling in one step. Unstyling removes ANSI sequences and leaves all other text.
↳ N-000618–N-000630

When not interactive, the text is written to standard output without launching any pager. Authors may pass a complete string, an iterator of chunks, or use a writable pager stream; all text written reaches the destination in order. Chunked pager output is flushed as it is written, so each chunk reaches the pager before the next chunk is requested. Styles are kept or stripped according to what that destination supports. A pager that writes to the process standard output does not close that real stream when it finishes.
↳ N-000631–N-000638

Authors may set a label: with no terminal that label is still printed once; an explicitly hidden bar prints nothing anywhere. ## Feature points

### FP-11: Terminal output and interaction helpers

**Public entry:** Echo (including to standard error), styling, styled echo, unstyling, pager output (including a writable pager stream), progress bars, reading a single character, pause until a key, launching an editor, launching an application, clearing the screen, looking up a per-user application config directory, wrapping text, opening files/streams (shared with FP-09), and binary/text standard-stream accessors.

**Normal behavior:**

It never adds styles to plain text. When the stream is not a terminal, ANSI styles in the text are stripped; when it is a terminal, styles are kept. The invocation may force color on (styles kept even when the stream is not a terminal), force color off (styles stripped even on a terminal), or leave autodetection; echo follows the color flag of the context current on its thread, and a thread that has not entered the context autodetects.
↳ N-000609–N-000617

- Styling wraps text with ANSI styles. Named foreground/background colors are the finite set: black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white, bright_black, bright_red, bright_green, bright_yellow, bright_blue, bright_magenta, bright_cyan, bright_white, and reset; a background color is styled differently from the same foreground color, and different names are styled differently. Color may also be an integer in 0–255 inclusive or a sequence of exactly three integers each in 0–255 inclusive (RGB). Independent style switches: bold, dim, underline, overline, italic, blink, reverse, strikethrough; each switch changes the styling, and a combination of switches differs from each switch alone. # Optlyn — Full Product Requirements Document

## Feature points

### FP-14: In-process runner

**Public entry:** Optlyn’s runner helpers: a runner that invokes a command with a list of argument tokens (and optional input, environment, program name, terminal width, color, and context settings) and a result object; an isolated-filesystem helper.
↳ N-000724, N-000725

**Normal behavior:**

- Invoking a command through the runner executes that command as if from the command line and returns a result that exposes: exit status, captured standard output (text and bytes), captured standard error separately (text and bytes), the combined captured output, and any exception raised by the callback.
↳ N-000726, N-000727

- Subcommands are selected by including their names in the argument token list.
↳ N-000728

- Extra keywords on invoke are passed as invocation-context settings. An environment supplied to one invoke applies to that invoke only.
↳ N-000729, N-000730

- Isolated filesystem: a context that sets the current working directory to a new empty directory. File-parameter commands can create and read files there without touching the original working directory. When no parent is given, the runner removes that directory on exit; when a parent path is supplied, the new directory is created as a child under that parent and is left in place. The new directory is always left in place after the block ends, so its files can still be inspected.
↳ N-000731–N-000733, N-001015

- Input supplied to invoke is fed to standard input. Visible prompts echo the typed line into the captured output; hidden prompts do not. An optional runner mode also echoes standard-input reads into captured output, not only prompt echoes: it echoes exactly the input that was actually read, never input that remained unread.
↳ N-000734–N-000736

Default capture does not provide a real file descriptor on those streams and does not record OS-level descriptor writes. Under file-descriptor capture the interpreter’s standard output and standard error streams report a real file descriptor, and OS-level writes to descriptor 1 are captured as standard output and those to descriptor 2 as standard error.
↳ N-000737–N-000741

**Boundary / error behavior:**

- The runner changes interpreter state and is not thread-safe.
↳ N-000742, N-000743

- If the command raises, the result still carries an exit status and the exception is inspectable on the result, unless the runner is told not to catch exceptions, in which case the exception propagates out of invoke. With standalone mode off, a raised exception is likewise inspectable on the result.
↳ N-000744–N-000747

- Isolated filesystem does not by itself mock Optlyn; commands that write files must actually write them inside the sandbox.
↳ N-000748, N-000749

- UNSETTLED: CF-000153 — N-000732 "When no parent is given, the runner removes that directory on exit" vs N-001015 "The new directory is always left in place after the block ends"
  rationale: Claim A says the runner removes the new directory on exit when no parent is given, while claim B says the new directory is always left in place after the block ends; for a directory created with no parent, both cannot hold.

**Public entry:** Standalone program invocation of any command or group; author-initiated clean stop and abort (including from confirm); conversion and usage failures from FP-03–FP-09.

↳ N-000711–N-000713

arguments.content:
# Implementation notes

Package: `src/optlyn` (src-layout, zero runtime dependencies, Python 3.10+).
Tests: `tests/test_optlyn_basics.py` (run with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest tests`).
Spec ids are cited in docstrings and comments as `# spec: N-xxxxxx`.

## Module map

| module | contents |
|---|---|
| `optlyn/__init__.py` | package-root exports (Contract 1) |
| `optlyn/commands.py` | `Command`, `Group`, `CommandCollection`, declaration decorators, ready-made option decorators, `pass_*` helpers, standalone `main` |
| `optlyn/core.py` | `Context`, `Parameter`, `Option`, `Argument`, `ParameterSource` |
| `optlyn/parser.py` | token parsing, argument assignment, value-source resolution, callbacks |
| `optlyn/paramtypes.py` | parameter types (renamed from `types.py` so it does not shadow the stdlib module) |
| `optlyn/termui.py` | terminal helpers, `open_file` and lazy/atomic file wrappers |
| `optlyn/formatting.py` | usage line, help page, `wrap_text` |
| `optlyn/shell_completion.py` | `{shell}_source` scripts and `{shell}_complete` suggestions |
| `optlyn/testing.py` | `CliRunner`, `Result`, `isolated_filesystem` |
| `optlyn/exceptions.py` | `OptlynError`, `UsageError`, `BadParameter`, `MissingParameter`, `NoSuchOption`, `Abort`, `Exit`, `FileError` |

## Choices where the spec disagrees or leaves room

Unsettled contradictions listed in `spec/MAP.md` (no human verdict; `--allow-open` export):

- **CF-000146 (deprecation warning channel).** N-000081 says stdout, N-000803 (channel table) says stderr. Chose **stderr**.
- **CF-000150 (env vs default map).** N-000230 ranks environment above the default map; N-000937 says default-map values beat environment. Chose **environment, then default map** (the FP-03 ranking), so `RETRIES=7` beats `default_map={"retries": 9}`.
- **CF-000151 (confirm answer that is neither yes nor no).** N-000495 says ask again; N-001016 says it counts as no. Chose **counts as no** (N-001016).
- **CF-000152 (default metavar for an integer option).** N-000326 says the type name (`INTEGER`); N-001013 (acceptance criterion) says `--count COUNT`. Chose the **destination name uppercased** (`COUNT`), matching the criterion. Choice types show their values as the metavar.
- **CF-000153 (isolated filesystem cleanup).** N-000732 says the directory is removed when no parent is given; N-001015 says it is always left in place. Chose **removed when no parent is given; left in place when a parent path is supplied**.
- **CF-000155 (default maximum content width).** FP-02 says 80; N-001014 says 100. Chose **80** (the more specific FP-02 statement). Set with `max_content_width`.

Other choices:

- **Confirmation prompts and `prompt_required`.** `prompt_required=True` (default) prompts when the option is omitted; `prompt_required=False` prompts only when the flag is given with no value (the spec's "does not require a prompt merely because omitted").
- **Chained subcommand arguments** end at the next token that names a subcommand of the chaining group.
- **Help and version callbacks** return the value they receive, so the flag's stored value stays boolean.
- **Deprecated parameters and commands** print a `DeprecationWarning:` line to stderr when the user supplies them.
- **Automatic help option** is placed first in the active parameter list, so an author option that reuses a help name wins that name and the other help names still print help.

## Known gaps

- **Feature-switch groups** (several options sharing one destination, FP-03): not implemented. The later declaration overwrites the earlier one.
- **`CliRunner(capture="fd")`** is accepted but behaves like `capture="sys"`; OS-level descriptor capture is not implemented.
- **Pager, editor, launch, and progress bar** helpers are minimal: they follow the stated contract on the paths exercised, but were not tested on a real terminal.
- **Group-level option mixing** (`allow_interspersed_args` on groups) is only exposed as the class attribute `interspersed_args`, not as a declaration keyword.
- **Wrapping** uses `textwrap`; the first-sentence ellipsis for short help is not implemented (the first sentence is used as is).
- **Checklist status.** The `spec/CHECKLIST.md` boxes are not ticked. Coverage is by implementation plus `# spec:` markers; the 10 tests cover the main paths, not every id. Ids without a marker should be treated as not individually verified.

steps.message:
Optlyn is built under `/app/src/optlyn` and imports from `PYTHONPATH=src`. Its 10 pytest checks pass, and four smoke scripts ran cleanly. I did not tick the checklist: most of the 1015 ids are implemented but only partly checked. Ids without a `# spec:` marker should be treated as not individually verified.

**What's in place**
- Commands, groups, chaining, and nested dispatch with eager `--help` and `--version`.
- Options and arguments: flags, on/off pairs, counting, repeatable and multi-value options, environment variables, default maps, prompts, and the password and confirmation options.
- Parameter types: Choice, IntRange, FloatRange, DateTime, Tuple, File, Path.
- Exit codes: 0 for success and intentional help, 2 for usage errors, 1 for abort and general errors.
- Terminal helpers, `CliRunner`, and shell completion for bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell.
- `pyproject.toml` (src-layout, zero dependencies, Python 3.10+), `NOTES.md`, and `tests/test_optlyn_basics.py`.

**Choices where the spec conflicts or leaves room** (all listed in `NOTES.md`)
- Deprecation warnings go to stderr.
- Environment variables beat the default map.
- A confirm answer other than yes or no counts as no.
- An integer option's metavar is the destination name (`--count COUNT`).
- Isolated filesystems are removed only when no parent path is given.
- Default maximum content width is 80.

**Known gaps**
- Feature-switch groups (several options sharing one destination) are not implemented; the later declaration wins.
- `CliRunner(capture="fd")` behaves like the default capture.
- Pager, editor, launch, and progress bar helpers are minimal and were not tried on a real terminal.

I also renamed the type module to `paramtypes.py`; a module called `types.py` shadows the stdlib when the package directory is on the path. I did not commit anything, since `/app` is not a git repository.
